The graph of the function $f(x)$ is shown above. 
Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=-1$ using a backward difference approximation with step size $h=2.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x)-f(x-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the point $x=-1.$ Applying the above formula with $x=-1$ and $h=2$ gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(-1) & ≈\frac{f(-1)-f(-1-2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{f(-1)-f(-3)}{2} \\  & =\frac{-1-(-2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
